text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has decided to introduce foreclosure laws to shift the burden of proof onto those accused of defaulting on repayment of bank loans.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the economy would be revived in three to six months while the new tax reforms would start yielding results in 12 to 18 months.
- A nine-hour power shutdown by the state-run Karachi Electric Supply Corporation resulted in losses of millions of rupees to industrial units in Karachi.
- State-run Pakistan Steel has asked the government for urgent financial assistance to save the country's largest industrial unit from imminent shut-down.
- The government has decided to set up a gas regulatory authority before going ahead with the privatisation of state-owned gas companies.
- The Privatisation Commission has decided to offer several entities for sale on a 100 percent down-payment basis.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has approved a 40-billion-rupee 700-megawatt Kohala hydel power project.

- An agreement was signed between Minorco Services of Netherlands, Northern Areas Administration and the Pakistan Mineral Development Corporation to explore for gold, platinum and other metals in the northern areas.
- Pakistan, along with Malaysia, Thailand and India, has complained to the Dispute Settlement body of the World Trade Organisation in Geneva over a U.S. shrimp import ban.
- Following the increase in support price of sunflower earlier this month, the price of locally produced sunflower oil is expected to rise by six rupees a kg, a study said.
- In a major departure from traditional budget-making, the government is to launch a three-way plan to reduce the fiscal deficit, stabilise standard tax rates and revitalise the banking sector.

- The government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will face a shortage of 100 billion rupees while preparing the budget due to non-commitment of aid from foreign donors at the Aid-to-Pakistan consortium meeting in Paris.

- The former chairman of the Karachi Port Trust, Vice Admiral (retd) Akbar H Khan and the divisional superintendent of Pakistan Railways, Karachi, M Rafique Dogar, have been arrested for alleged involvement in the sale of valuable land at throwaway prices.
- The Central Board of Revenue has suspended four senior customs officers for their alleged involvement in clearance of containers against false documents.
